docs.text: casapi ¶ Stateless HTTP API for remote Claude Code execution powered by Claude Agent SDK. Capabilities ¶ POST /v1/query : run one ephemeral agent query and receive the result and full message transcript as JSON. POST /v1/query/stream : the same run streamed as Server-Sent Events. GET /v1/info and GET /health . Bearer-token authentication, workspace confinement, opt-in bypassPermissions , concurrency and timeout limits. No sessions, resume, or server-side conversation state. Development ¶ uv sync uv run uvicorn casapi.main:app --host 127 .0.0.1 --port 8000 API reference Deployment The original repository is licensed under AGPL-3.0-only.

docs.text: Deployment ¶ Local development ¶ uv sync CASAPI_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED = true uv run uvicorn casapi.main:app --host 127 .0.0.1 --port 8000 Remote server ¶ Install dependencies on the server: git clone https://github.com/dceoy/casapi.git /opt/casapi cd /opt/casapi && uv sync --no-dev Authenticate Claude on the server. The SDK spawns the Claude Code CLI, so either set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment file below, or log in once with claude as the user that runs the service. Create /etc/casapi.env (mode 0600 ): CASAPI_API_KEY = <long random secret, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32 > CASAPI_WORKSPACE_ROOT = /srv/workspaces ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = sk-ant-... Run uvicorn on loopback or a private interface, and expose it only through TLS (a reverse proxy) or a private network such as Tailscale or an SSH tunnel ( ssh -L 8000:127.0.0.1:8000 server ). Disable proxy response buffering for /v1/query/stream (casapi sends X-Accel-Buffering: no ). Run it as an unprivileged user that owns only the workspace directory. Workspace confinement limits the starting cwd , not what Bash can reach. The agent inherits this environment file, so a run can read CASAPI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from its own environment — the API key is effectively a shell as this user (see the README security model). The concurrency limit is per process: running uvicorn with --workers N multiplies CASAPI_MAX_CONCURRENCY by N. systemd unit ¶ [Unit] Description = casapi After = network-online.target [Service] User = casapi WorkingDirectory = /opt/casapi EnvironmentFile = /etc/casapi.env ExecStart = /opt/casapi/.venv/bin/uvicorn casapi.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 Restart = on-failure NoNewPrivileges = true [Install] WantedBy = multi-user.target Client smoke test ¶ From the client machine (here via an SSH tunnel on localhost:8000 ): curl -sS http://localhost:8000/health curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/info -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASAPI_API_KEY " curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASAPI_API_KEY " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"prompt": "Reply with the single word: pong", "max_turns": 1}' A 200 response with "result": "pong" confirms authentication, Claude credentials, and the SDK/CLI path all work.

docs.text: REST API ¶ All /v1/* endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <CASAPI_API_KEY> . FastAPI also serves /docs and /openapi.json . Statelessness contract ¶ Every request is one ephemeral SDK query() run. The server keeps no sessions and offers no resume, continue, or fork. The session_id in responses is informational only and cannot be sent back: request bodies with unknown fields (such as resume or session_id ) are rejected with 422 . To continue work, include the needed context in the next prompt. Runs are hermetic. CLI session persistence is disabled, so the CLI writes no resumable transcript, and host and project settings are not loaded ( setting_sources is empty): hooks, MCP servers, and permission rules from the host's or the workspace's .claude/settings.json never enter a run. Auto memory is disabled ( CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 ), and MCP configuration is strict and isolated. Managed policy settings and ~/.claude.json still load. What persists after a run is only what the agent itself writes — files in the workspace and ordinary CLI bookkeeping under ~/.claude . GET /health ¶ No authentication. { "status" : "ok" } GET /v1/info ¶ { "version" : "0.1.0" , "stateless" : true , "default_model" : null , "workspace_root" : "/srv/workspaces" , "default_permission_mode" : "acceptEdits" , "default_allowed_tools" : [ "Read" , "Write" , "Edit" , "Bash" , "Glob" , "Grep" ], "max_concurrency" : 4 , "auth_required" : true } POST /v1/query ¶ Request (only prompt is required): { "prompt" : "List the Python files" , "system_prompt" : null , "model" : null , "cwd" : "myproject" , "allowed_tools" : [ "Read" , "Glob" ], "disallowed_tools" : null , "permission_mode" : "default" , "max_turns" : 5 , "max_budget_usd" : 1.0 , "effort" : "low" , "timeout_seconds" : 300 } cwd : relative to CASAPI_WORKSPACE_ROOT , or absolute inside it. system_prompt : when omitted, the run uses the Claude Code preset system prompt. Send a string to replace it. allowed_tools : an auto-approve list, not a restriction. It names tools the run may use without a permission decision; it does not remove other tools, and file edits are still approved under acceptEdits . When omitted, the server default ( CASAPI_ALLOWED_TOOLS ) applies — a default, not a ceiling. permission_mode : default , acceptEdits , plan , bypassPermissions (requires server opt-in), dontAsk , auto . max_turns : 1–1000. max_budget_usd and timeout_seconds must be > 0; timeout_seconds may not exceed CASAPI_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS . If the client disconnects, the run is promptly cancelled and its concurrency slot is freed. The server internally answers 499 without logging an error; the response is not delivered to the disconnected client. Response: { "result" : "There are 3 Python files." , "session_id" : "0b0e..." , "subtype" : "success" , "is_error" : false , "num_turns" : 2 , "duration_ms" : 4210 , "duration_api_ms" : 3900 , "total_cost_usd" : 0.0123 , "usage" : { "input_tokens" : 100 , "output_tokens" : 40 }, "stop_reason" : "end_turn" , "messages" : [ { "type" : "system" , "subtype" : "init" , "data" : {} }, { "type" : "assistant" , "model" : "..." , "content" : [ { "type" : "thinking" , "thinking" : "..." , "signature" : "..." }, { "type" : "tool_use" , "id" : "t1" , "name" : "Glob" , "input" : { "pattern" : "*.py" } } ], "error" : null , "usage" : null , "stop_reason" : null , "session_id" : null , "uuid" : null }, { "type" : "user" , "content" : [ { "type" : "tool_result" , "tool_use_id" : "t1" , "content" : "a.py" , "is_error" : false } ], "uuid" : null , "parent_tool_use_id" : null }, { "type" : "result" , "subtype" : "success" , "is_error" : false , "result" : "..." , "session_id" : "0b0e..." , "num_turns" : 2 , "duration_ms" : 4210 , "duration_api_ms" : 3900 , "total_cost_usd" : 0.0123 , "usage" : null , "stop_reason" : "end_turn" , "errors" : null } ] } An agent-level failure ( is_error: true , e.g. subtype: "error_max_turns" ) is still HTTP 200 . Message types not listed above are emitted as {"type": "<snake_case_class>", "data": {...}} . POST /v1/query/stream ¶ Same request body. All validation (auth, cwd , permissions, concurrency) happens before streaming starts, so those failures are ordinary HTTP errors. The response is text/event-stream ; each SDK message is one event: data: {"type": "system", "subtype": "init", "data": {}} data: {"type": "assistant", "content": [...]} data: {"type": "result", "subtype": "success", "result": "..."} If the runner fails or times out mid-stream, one final event is sent and the stream ends: data: {"type": "error", "detail": "agent run timed out"} Treat a run as successful only when a result event arrives. A stream that ends without one — including a run whose message stream stops early — closes with an error event instead. During idle periods the stream sends an SSE comment : heartbeat every 15 seconds; clients must ignore comment lines. Disconnecting from this endpoint cancels the run and releases its slot. The run deadline also cancels the run and releases its slot if the client stops reading. For an abandoned stream, the run timeout initiates cancellation, but awaited SDK shutdown can extend beyond it. Errors ¶ Status Meaning 400 cwd missing or not a directory; timeout_seconds above server max 401 Missing or incorrect bearer token 403 cwd outside workspace root; bypassPermissions not enabled 422 Invalid body (empty prompt, unknown/stateful fields, bad ranges) 429 Concurrency limit reached 502 SDK/CLI failure, or the run ended without a result message 503 CASAPI_API_KEY not configured and unauthenticated access not allowed 504 Run exceeded its timeout Errors use FastAPI's {"detail": "..."} body.
